clue.text: Popular wine put behind bars

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A well-liked wine gets locked away in a cellar, as if jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is the British name for Rhine wine. The phrase IN HOCK is slang for being in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in hock is informal slang for being in jail, so it matches someone imprisoned.

clue.text: Blue recess housing this in Notre Dame

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an indent is a recess or notch
ce is French for 'this', the language spoken at Notre Dame

explanation.surface: Something risqué tucked into an alcove of the Paris cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Notre Dame signals French, so 'this' is translated into French; the clue's blue means smutty, not sad or the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is an informal word for rude or smutty, as in blue jokes or films, which are indecent.

clue.text: Carefully select some bananas and cream

parts.note: a hand is a cluster of bananas growing together
the cream of something is its best part, the pick

explanation.surface: Choosing ingredients for a dessert of bananas and cream.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas and cream reads as a pudding, but 'some bananas' is a bunch called a hand, and cream is the best, the pick.
explanation.definitionFit: To handpick is to choose individually with personal care rather than at random.

clue.text: Queen's favourite decor, gilded walls

indicators.note: walls enclose a space, so the wanted letters are enclosed within the neighbouring words

parts.note: runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: The late Queen preferred gilt walls in her palace decor.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept many Welsh corgis, the dog breed she was most associated with.

clue.text: Element in rugby mostly getting negligible examination

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the scrum is a set piece in rugby
negligible means very small

explanation.surface: Part of a rugby match receives hardly any analysis from the pundits.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, critical inspection of something, the same as careful examination.

clue.text: October alas misjudged for popular form of retail?

indicators.note: something misjudged has been got wrong, so these letters are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper laments a poorly timed autumn sales push.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAR BOOT SALE is a British outdoor market where people sell unwanted goods from the boots (trunks) of their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Car boot sales are a hugely popular informal way for ordinary people to sell second-hand goods.

clue.text: Rising heat with ten playing to magnify the risk

parts.note: rising means going up

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about and being rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Temperatures climb while the team of ten plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake; raising it means increasing what is at stake or risked.

clue.text: Is friend boycotting Northern island?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to boycott is to stay away from, so the named letter is kept out

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate)
standard abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pal is shunning some northern isle.
explanation.walkthrough: China meaning mate comes from Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate'. ISCHIA is an island in the Bay of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is a volcanic island off the coast near Naples, in Italy.

clue.text: Emitting painful expression, sensational journalist made loud noise

indicators.note: emitting means sending out, so those letters are let out of the word

parts.note: yellow journalism is sensationalist reporting
a cry of pain
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A tabloid hack cries out in pain and makes a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout out loudly, so having yelled means having raised a loud noise.

clue.text: Hollywood star captivated by sudden irony

indicators.note: held captive by the words that follow, so the answer is enclosed within them

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A film actor is charmed by an unexpected twist of irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is an Oscar-winning American film actor, a major name of the movies.

clue.text: Body of rules confused poor clot

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up and need sorting into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hapless idiot is baffled by the rulebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A protocol is a formal set of procedures or etiquette governing conduct, a code of regulations.

clue.text: Model exuding energy and bit of chic I love in free work?

indicators.note: exuding means giving off, so that letter leaves the name

parts.note: Caprice Bourret is a well-known fashion model
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: just a small bit, meaning only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A model sheds her energy but keeps a hint of chic, adoring a free outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively musical piece in free form, so it is work unbound by strict rules.

clue.text: Minor training with no gender bias?

definitions.text: Minor training with no gender bias?

parts.words: Minor training with no gender bias?
parts.note: surface reading: some small, minor bit of staff training on equality
setter's reading: the schooling of minors, children, with boys and girls taught together

explanation.walkthrough: Minor looks like 'slight', but it is the noun for a child, so this is about how children are schooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed schooling teaches boys and girls in the same classes, treating both sexes alike.

clue.text: Love of old Corsica among natives — it marked out Napoleon?

parts.note: an ex is a former lover
Corsica's natives speak French, in which an island is an île

explanation.surface: Napoleon's old love for his native Corsica set him apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was born on Corsica, a French island, and was later banished to Elba and then St Helena.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon is famous for his banishment to Elba and St Helena, so enforced absence characterised his later life.

clue.text: Rider's condition key perhaps with loss of energy later

parts.note: in good nick means in good condition

indicators.note: loss means something is taken away, so one letter goes missing

parts.note: a skeleton key opens many locks
E for energy, the later of the two in the word

explanation.surface: A jockey's fitness, like a key, may decline with lost energy later in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In good nick' is British for in good shape. NICK SKELTON is a British showjumper who won Olympic gold in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Skelton is a celebrated equestrian, a showjumping horseman, so he is a famous rider.

clue.text: Rearrange messy site and impose order

indicators.note: rearrange tells us directly to set the letters in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to tidy up an untidy building site.
explanation.definitionFit: To systemise is to arrange according to a method, bringing structure and organisation where it was lacking.

clue.text: No good line occupying discussion — that's characteristic of the English?

indicators.note: occupying a space means sitting inside it, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: a moot is a meeting or debate
taken as written
standard abbreviation for good
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A bad line in a debate is said to typify English people.
explanation.walkthrough: The English are stereotyped as speaking no language but their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoglot speaks only one language, a trait jokingly attributed to the English abroad.

clue.text: Plain like some medicine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bare and functional, unadorned
second meaning: describing medicine practised at the bedside

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers austere surroundings and the branch of medicine dealing with patients directly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stark and efficient, and also relates to the direct treatment of patients.

clue.text: Meaty item found in list following South African custom

indicators.note: following means coming after, so that piece is placed at the end

parts.note: standard abbreviation
usage is established custom or practice
a roll is a register or list

explanation.surface: A South African tradition is recorded in a list of meat dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: A SAUSAGE ROLL is a British snack of sausage meat wrapped in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage meat baked in pastry makes a savoury snack, so it is a meat-filled food.

clue.text: PM put on edge in chaos

indicators.note: in a down answer, put on means placed above, so one piece sits over the other

parts.note: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is on edge amid political turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem means violent disorder or confusion, a near synonym for complete disorder.

clue.text: Country singer switching centre for proprietor

indicators.note: switching the middle letters means swapping their order around

parts.note: Dolly Parton is a country music star

explanation.surface: A country star changes position at centre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron can be the owner of a business such as a restaurant, a usage borrowed from French.

clue.text: Come to a train

parts.note: taken as written
a wake is the trail left behind a moving ship

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to turn up to a waiting railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: Come to a train looks like arriving for a rail journey; 'come to' is the definition, meaning regain consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness after fainting, which is to rouse oneself from sleep or stupor.

clue.text: Writer, maybe, chap with a lot of sense in article

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: nous is common sense
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A sensible fellow appears in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer is defined by example: a noun naming one who does an action, formed from write plus -er.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent noun denotes the doer of an action, such as writer from write or baker from bake.

clue.text: Pavarotti, say, vocalised note

indicators.note: vocalised means spoken out, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: The great opera singer belts out a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical, but it is a banknote: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was a famous Italian operatic singer with the high male voice.

clue.text: Awful choir off-key imbibing religious instruction by fellow

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so other letters go inside
singing off-key is out of tune, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is placed alongside another

parts.note: RI is the school subject abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A choir sings out of tune during a scripture lesson with one of the dons.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the old name for religious education in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrific means shockingly dreadful, terrible enough to cause horror.

clue.text: Note limited group that's divided city as a whole

indicators.note: something divided is split apart, letting other letters sit in the gap

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nota bene, take note
a lot is a set of items

explanation.surface: A small group splits the city, like Berlin's Cold War wall.
explanation.walkthrough: EC, the City of London's postcode area, is a standard crossword device for 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is French borrowed into English, meaning all together, treated as one unit.

clue.text: Old artist in collection ultimately kept by loaded magnate

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so that letter goes into the other word
loaded can mean drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wealthy tycoon keeps a Renaissance painting in his collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' suggests wealth to go with magnate, but it signals the reordering.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Mantegna was an Italian Renaissance painter of the fifteenth century, an Old Master.

clue.text: Inhuman routine in scientific establishment retracted

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
retracted means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: short for laboratory
a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: Cruel experiments are withdrawn from a research facility.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal means savagely cruel, lacking any humane feeling or compassion.
